segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: At the very end, Jesus knew everything had now been accomplished. He wasn't a victim losing a fight — he was finishing a work.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: With his last breath he spoke three words that weren't a cry of defeat, but a declaration of completion.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: It is finished. Not I am finished. The thing he came to do was done — completed, paid in full, nothing left owing.

segments.speaker: jesus
segments.text: Father, into thy hands I commend my spirit.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The last words he said were words of trust, spoken to the Father he had been talking to all night.

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: And he bowed his head, and gave up the ghost.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he bowed his head and gave up the spirit — on his own terms, not theirs. Nobody took his life from him. He laid it down.

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: And, behold, the veil of the temple was rent in twain from the top to the bottom.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: At that moment, in the temple across the city, the great veil that walled off the holiest place was torn in two, from the top down —

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: as if torn by a hand from above.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: That curtain had kept people out of God's presence for centuries. The instant he died, it was ripped open.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The way in was thrown wide — for everyone.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The curtain that kept you out was torn open the moment he died. The way to God is open. Walk in.
